_comment: Example Claude Code settings showing ONLY what herdr-control needs.
Do NOT copy this over your own ~/.claude/settings.json — that file holds your
model, permissions, env and possibly secrets. Either run ./install.sh --apply
(which merges just these entries and backs up first), or hand-merge the
"hooks" block below into your existing settings.
Replace __HERDR_CONTROL__ with the absolute path to your checkout.
install.sh does this substitution for you.
async:true matters — these run on every tool call and must never block the
agent. herdr-resolve exits in ~4ms when there is nothing pending.
SessionStart is deliberately async:false — its whole job is to inject
additionalContext before the session's first turn, which an async
('deferred') hook is not guaranteed to do in time.
_sandbox_note: If you run Claude Code with its filesystem/network sandbox enabled, the
herdr socket and your tmux socket must be reachable or pane resolution
Without the tmux socket the alert can still be sent, but it cannot work out
WHICH pane asked, so replies have nowhere to go.
